issue.title: fix(metro-config): Fix module debug strings being kept by noxcturnal in production
issue.body:
## Summary

We keep a debug string on Metro output `require` calls, such as `require(deps[0], "react");` to name dependency requests when they fail. This is only done in development for Babel but was erroneously still turned on in production for noxcturnal.

The corresponding plugin also generated dependency-map references in some cases where module wrapping was disabled.

## Set of changes

- Production imports, re-exports, and helpers now consistently omit debug names.
- Async imports, maybe-sync imports, and prefetch calls follow the same rule
- Development and optional-dependency diagnostics retain names, as expected
- Disabling module wrapping now preserves source-based loads (bail case)

issue.title: [expo-audio][iOS] `play()` silently stalls when it overlaps the delayed session deactivation after `pause()` or finish

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: Issue is ready to be reviewed by a maintainer

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: S2 - Medium: narrower breakage, or common breakage with a reasonable workaround.

issue.body: ## Summary On iOS, expo-audio deactivates the audio session 100 ms after a player pauses or finishes. If another player's `play()` lands around that deactivation, the new player silently stays paused. There is no error, `playing` and `isBuffering` are both `false`, and `currentTime` stays at 0. In my tests it didn't recover by itself within 2.5 s. This hits apps that play short clips one after another, because the next clip can start about 100 ms after the previous one ends. JS has no signal for it, so an app needs its own watchdog just to notice. A plain `AVPlayer` with the same session lifecycle stalls the same way, with no expo-audio code involved. So the underlying behavior looks like iOS, and expo-audio's deactivation timing is what triggers it. Whether iOS treats this as a bug or as expected, I don't know. ## Minimal reproducible example https://github.com/kockar96/expo-audio-session-repro ## Steps to reproduce The repro has a small native control module, so it needs a device build. I saw no stall in the simulator while investigating this in my app, so please use a physical iPhone. 1. Clone the repo, then set your own `ios.bundleIdentifier` and `ios.appleTeamId` in `app.json`. 2. Run `npm install`. 3. Run `npx expo run:ios --device --configuration Release --no-bundler`. 4. With the phone unlocked, run `scripts/run-arm.sh E0 3 e0`. Results land in `out/`. 5. Run `python3 scripts/analyze.py 'out/results-*.jsonl'`. Each trial: 1. Creates two loaded players from the same local 0.6 s clip, in `playsInSilentMode` + `mixWithOthers` mode. 2. Plays the first until it pauses (`pause`) or finishes naturally (`finish`). 3. Waits a gap from 0 to 300 ms. 4. Calls `await second.seekTo(0)`, then `second.play()`. 5. Counts a stall if `currentTime` hasn't moved 2.5 s later. **Expected:** the second player starts, as it does at most gaps outside the window (about 130 ms median to first progress). **Actual:** around the 100 ms mark, the second player usually never starts. ## Results iPhone 13 on iOS 27.0, Release build. The gaps deliberately target the window, so these rates are far above what an app would see in normal use. The raw data is in the repo. | Variant | Stalls | |---|---| | expo-audio | 24/72 | | expo-audio with an idle `keepAudioSessionActive` player | 0/144 | | Plain `AVPlayer`, deactivating like expo-audio | 40/144 | | Plain `AVPlayer`, no deactivation | 0/72 | Stalls by gap for unmodified expo-audio (`pause` + `finish`, 6 trials per gap): | Gap (ms) | 0–60 | 80 | 90 | 100 | 110 | 120 | 140 | 170 | 200 | 300 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Stalls | 0 | 1 | 5 | 6 | 6 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | I also timestamped `play()` and the deactivation in an instrumented build (68/144 stalls at baseline): | When the second `play()` was called | Stalls | |---|---| | Before the guard, and the guard saw it playing (deactivation skipped) | 0/36 | | Before the guard, but the guard saw it not playing yet | 16/18 | | During `setActive(false)` | 42/44 | | After `setActive(false)` returned | 10/46 | Across this build and the cancel-on-play build below, nearly all stalls in the last row came within about 17 ms of the return (23 of 24). `setActive(false)` itself took about 50 ms at the median and up to about 675 ms. In the plain `AVPlayer` control, no deactivation reported an error, and stalled players were left with `timeControlStatus` paused and no waiting reason. ## Possible fixes I tried Both were tested as local patches to `AudioModule.swift` ([patch](https://github.com/kockar96/expo-audio-session-repro/blob/main/patches/expo-audio-instrumentation.patch)), against the 68/144 baseline: | Change | Stalls | |---|---| | Cancel the pending deactivation when a newer `play()` arrives | 58/144 | | Skip the deactivation in `mixWithOthers` mode | 2/144 | **Cancelling isn't enough.** It removes the stalls where the deactivation is cancelled (0/59), but a `play()` during `setActive(false)` still stalls (43/45). **Skipping looks like the better direction for mixable sessions.** A mixable session doesn't interrupt other apps, so as far as I can tell the deactivation doesn't give anything back. You may have reasons for it that I can't see. The change was: ```swift private func deactivateSession() { if case .mixWithOthers = interruptionMode { return } // existing delayed deactivation } ``` I only tested the stall, not the effect on interruption handling, mode changes or other modules. I'm happy to open a PR if this direction works for you, or to use whatever you prefer. For example, `setAudioSessionOwner()` in [#52471](https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/52471) could cover this too, though the app would have to opt in. ## Open questions and limits - All of this comes from one iPhone 13 on iOS 27.0, on the device's default audio route, with no other audio app running. - The plain `AVPlayer` control calls `play()`, while expo-audio calls `playImmediately(atRate:)`. - The 2 stalls left by the `mixWithOthers` patch were both on the first trial after launch. That first trial stalled in 6 of 8 keeperless expo-audio runs (including patched builds), 0 of 5 plain `AVPlayer` runs and 0 of 3 keeper runs. I don't know the cause and it may be a separate issue. ## Why this matters in a real app We hit this in [Sugu](https://sugu.now), a language-learning app that plays short audio clips of words and phrases. Learners often play several in quick succession, for example: - **Tapping through a word list.** Each row in our vocabulary search has an audio button, and people tap one, then the next, then the next. - **Practice exercises.** Word audio plays as exercises change, so a new clip can start right after the previous one ended or was cut off. Occasionally a clip starts about a second late. That delay is our own 800 ms watchdog recovering the stalled player. Without a watchdog, I'd expect silence, as in the repro. In that list, on the same iPhone in a Release build, I measured 118 plays from automated taps across six rows, about 1.5 s apart, with no artificial load. Two stalled at position 0 and started only after the watchdog recovered them, about 1.1 s after the request. The median was about 220 ms. I also drove our playback engine directly with repeated plays, without the UI: | Build | Without keeper | With keeper | |---|---|---| | Dev | 6/120 | 0/120 | | Release, JS thread kept busy for up to 200 ms | 5/160 | 0/160 | | Release, idle | 0/120 | 0/120 | "Keeper" is our current workaround: one empty `keepAudioSessionActive` player kept alive in the foreground. I haven't measured the word list with the keeper. The app was on expo-audio 58.0.9, whose session code matches the 58.0.11 used in the repro. ## Related - [#52471](https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/52471): the same delayed deactivation interrupts expo-video. Proposes `setAudioSessionOwner()`. - [#38671](https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/38671), [#39250](https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/39250): expo-audio pausing expo-video, and the origin of `keepAudioSessionActive`. - [#47045](https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/47045): the same back-to-back clip pattern, with a different symptom (main-thread hang). - [#44914](https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/44914): a comment there attributes truncated recordings to the same deactivation. - [#48532](https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/48532): an earlier PR that included a token to supersede stale deactivations, an idea it credits to [#47079](https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/47079). I didn't find an existing report of this specific stall, but I may have missed one. ## Environment ```text expo-env-info 2.2.1 environment info: System: OS: macOS 27.0.1 Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 24.22.2 npm: 11.19.1 Managers: CocoaPods: 1.17.0 SDKs: iOS SDK: Platforms: DriverKit 27.2, iOS 27.2, macOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, watchOS 27.2 IDEs: Android Studio: 2026.2 AI-262.10968.63.2622.16730706 Xcode: 27.2/27B52 - /usr/bin/xcodebuild npmPackages: expo: ~58.0.23 => 58.0.23 react: 19.3.0 => 19.3.0 react-native: 0.88.1 => 0.88.1 npmGlobalPackages: eas-cli: 20.0.0 Expo Workflow: managed ``` expo-audio 58.0.11. Tested on a physical iPhone 13, iOS 27.0 (24A437). ## Expo Doctor Diagnostics ```text Running 20 checks on your project... 20/20 checks passed. No issues detected! ```

issue.body:
### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/azarzalejoefy/expo-go-58-cold-deeplink

### Steps to reproduce

The repro is `npx create-expo-app --template blank@sdk-58` plus `expo-linking`. `App.js` prints the launch URL three ways.

1. `npm install && npx expo start --port 8081`
2. On an iOS simulator with Expo Go 58.0.7, make sure Expo Go is **not running**: `xcrun simctl terminate booted host.exp.Exponent`
3. `xcrun simctl openurl booted "exp://127.0.0.1:8081/--/some/path?x=1"`

**Expected:** `getInitialURL()`, `getLinkingURL()` and `useLinkingURL()` all return `exp://127.0.0.1:8081/--/some/path?x=1`.

**Observed** (Expo Go 58.0.7, iPhone 16e simulator, iOS 26.2):

```
getInitialURL(): exp://127.0.0.1:8081/--/some/path?x=1
getLinkingURL(): null
useLinkingURL(): null
```

Then, with the experience still running, opening `exp://127.0.0.1:8081/--/other/path` does not update `useLinkingURL()` either.

**Impact on Expo Router:** on iOS, `expo-router`'s `getInitialURL` (`build/link/linking.js`) reads `getLinkingURL()`, so a cold-start deep link opens the app at `/` instead of the linked screen.
- This breaks Maestro/E2E flows that start with `openLink` into Expo Go.
- In our own Expo Router app (not the repro), the same cold start opened the linked screen on SDK 57 with Expo Go 57.0.9. On SDK 58 it opens `/`, with Expo Go 58.0.5 and with 58.0.7.
- A native release build of that app on SDK 58 (expo 58.0.17 and 58.0.22) keeps the path on a cold start (its own custom scheme). So this looks specific to the Expo Go host.

issue.title: Fix builds and tests for React Native 0.89

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: ExpoBot has some suggestions

issue.body:
# Why

These break with React Native 0.89.0-rc.0:

- Nullability (facebook/react-native#59405): `constantsToExport()` is non-optional. This breaks the `lottie-react-native` Swift override and an `expo-dev-launcher` iOS test.
- Deprecated JNI overload: `react-native-maps` ships pre-generated JNI code that calls the deprecated `invokeJavaMethod`. React Native compiles it with `-Werror`.
- Removed APIs: `getDevServerSplitBundleURL` (facebook/react-native#58556) in `expo-dev-launcher`. `RCTEnableTurboModule` (facebook/react-native#59440), `RCTModuleData.h` (facebook/react-native#59426), and `-[RCTBridge devSettings]` (facebook/react-native#59443) in Expo Go.
- Kotlin 2.3: `kotlinOptions` is an error in `expo-brownfield`. A new type inference warning fails the `expo-modules-core` and `expo-media-library` Android tests, which use `allWarningsAsErrors`. Kotlin 2.3 also compiles inherited interface default methods as bridge methods. `AppContext` inherits `findView` and `assertMainThread` from `ConverterContext`, and MockK cannot stub bridge methods, so 297 of 304 `expo-modules-core` instrumentation tests fail in their shared setup.
- `@react-native/jest-preset` sets its transform to a resolved `babel-jest` path (facebook/react-native#58598). `jest-expo` matched only `'babel-jest'`, so the upstream transform stayed first and every Jest suite failed.
- `PlatformColor` attributes that resolve to a ColorStateList now return the list's default color (facebook/react-native@4d536fa8cd). Before, React Native returned `TypedValue.data`, which is not a color. An `expo-modules-core` test expected the old value.
- NDK: React Native 0.89 uses NDK 28.2 and fbjni 0.8.1. Expo Go Android hardcoded NDK 27.1, so it crashed at startup: `cannot locate symbol "__cxa_init_primary_exception" referenced by libfbjni.so`.

# How

- pnpm patches: `lottie-react-native` returns `[AnyHashable: Any]`, the same change as the upstream fix lottie-react-native/lottie-react-native#1486. `react-native-maps` calls the new `invokeJavaMethod` overload on React Native 0.89+ behind a version guard, the same change as react-native-maps/react-native-maps#6048.
- `expo-dev-launcher`: remove the override, and remove `!` in the test.
- Expo Go iOS: remove `RCTEnableTurboModule` and its unused parameter, remove the dead `RCTModuleData.h` imports, and get `RCTDevSettings` with `moduleForClass:`.
- Expo Go Android: set `ndkVersion` to React Native's `28.2.13676358`.
- `expo-brownfield`: use `kotlin { compilerOptions { jvmTarget } }` in the plugin template and in minimal-tester, and regenerate `build.gradle.patch`.
- `expo-modules-core`: override `findView` and `assertMainThread` in `AppContext` and call `super`. An explicit override compiles to a normal method, so MockK can stub it. The behavior does not change.
- Android tests: give explicit type arguments (`<Either<Int, String>, Any>`, `arrayOf<Any?>`), and expect the ColorStateList default color. Expo passes `PlatformColor` to React Native's `ColorPropConverter`, so Expo modules get the fix with no code change.
- `jest-expo`: also match `babel-jest` resolved from the preset's directory.

Not in this PR: React Native 0.89 deprecates `<cxxreact/ReactNativeVersion.h>` in favor of `<React/Utils.h>` (facebook/react-native#58403). `expo-modules-jsi` still includes the old header, so the iOS build prints the deprecation warning 18 times. The `expo-modules-jsi` SwiftPM build does not have `<React/Utils.h>` in its header search paths, so the switch needs build changes in `Package.swift`, `build-swiftpm-app-phase.sh`, and `CustomBuild.ts`. A follow-up PR will do it. This PR adds and then reverts a first attempt that only changed the include.

Stack:
1. #52968: datetimepicker 9.2.2
2. #52977: upgrade React Native to 0.89.0-rc.0
3. This PR

# Test Plan

- minimal-tester: builds and runs on the iOS simulator and the Android emulator.
- bare-expo: builds and runs on both. On Android, Lottie, SVG, and DateTimePicker (the native picker opens) work.
- Expo Go iOS: builds, and Home loads. native-component-list in Expo Go shows Lottie, SVG, Maps, and DateTimePicker.
- Expo Go Android: builds with NDK 28.2, and Home loads. With NDK 27.1 it crashed at startup.
- Jest: `expo-linking` (4/4 suites), `jest-expo` (28/28), and `expo-asset` (27/27) pass. They failed before.
- Android: all modules' unit tests compile (`compileDebugUnitTestKotlin --continue`), and `ColorTypeConverterTest` passes (54/54).
- `expo-modules-core` instrumentation tests on the Android emulator: 304/304 pass. Before the `AppContext` change, 297 failed.

## Known CI failures

These 2 checks fail.

- `test (22)`, `test (24)` (Create Expo Module): the e2e creates a module from this branch's template, but installs `jest-expo` from npm. The published `jest-expo` 58 only accepts `@react-native/jest-preset@^0.88.1`, and the template now uses 0.89.0-rc.0, so `npm install` fails with `ERESOLVE`. #52990 makes the e2e use the workspace `jest-expo`. In a local run on this stack, the e2e then passes (47/47).

# Screenshots

No UI change.

# Checklist

- [x] I added a changeset and followed [this short guide](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-before-submitting)
- [ ] This diff will work correctly for `npx expo prebuild` & EAS Build (eg: updated a module plugin).
- [ ] Conforms with the [Documentation Writing Style Guide](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/main/guides/Expo%20Documentation%20Writing%20Style%20Guide.md)

issue.body:
### Summary

When the app runs right-to-left (e.g. app language Hebrew), the floating Tools button is **drawn** on the left, but `DevMenuFABWindow` still **accepts touches** at its unmirrored (right-hand) frame. So:

- taps on app controls under the invisible right-hand rect never reach the app (in our app: the header avatar on every screen);
- the visible button can't be tapped or dragged — touches on it go straight through to the app.

LTR is fine. Re-files #51000 (same root cause), which was closed automatically for having no repro — this one has a minimal repro and a verified one-line fix.

### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/yuval-blink/expo-dev-menu-fab-rtl-repro — `create-expo-app --template blank-typescript@sdk-57` + `expo-dev-client`, plus:
- `App.tsx`: two LTR-pinned pads across the top, LEFT and RIGHT, each with a tap counter;
- `app.json`: `ios.infoPlist.CFBundleLocalizations: ["en", "he"]`.

### Steps

1. `bun install && npx expo run:ios`
2. Switch the app to Hebrew and relaunch:
   `xcrun simctl spawn booted defaults write com.example.fabrtlrepro AppleLanguages -array he`
   (the screen shows `I18nManager.isRTL = true`).
3. The Tools button appears at the top **left** (its default position is top right).
4. Tap the RIGHT pad near the top-right corner → counter stays at 0. Taps on RIGHT away from that corner do count.
5. Tap the gear → the menu doesn't open; the tap lands on LEFT (its counter goes up). Dragging the gear doesn't move it either.
6. Switch back to `en` → the gear is top right, opens the menu, and both pads count as expected.

**Expected:** the button's hit area matches where it's drawn in RTL too.
**Actual:** the hit area is the horizontal mirror of the drawn button.

![comparison](https://github.com/yuval-blink/expo-dev-menu-fab-rtl-repro/blob/main/screenshots/comparison.png?raw=true)
*Left: RTL, unpatched (red = where touches are actually captured). Middle: LTR. Right: RTL with the fix below.*

### Cause

- `ios/FAB/DevMenuFABView.swift` draws the pill with `.position(x: currentFrame.midX, y: currentFrame.midY)` and reports `onFrameChange(CGRect(origin: position, size: fabSize))`. Nothing under `ios/FAB/` sets a layout direction, so under RTL SwiftUI mirrors `.position`'s x-axis, while the reported rect stays in physical (unmirrored) coordinates.
- `ios/FAB/DevMenuFABWindow.swift` stores that rect as `fabFrame`, and `hitTest` only forwards touches inside `fabFrame.insetBy(dx: -10, dy: -10)`. So it captures the unmirrored rect (where nothing is drawn) and passes the drawn button's touches through to the app.

The edge-snapping and default-position math (`snapToEdge`, `defaultPosition`, `edgeTranslation`) is already physical, so the view just shouldn't be mirrored.

### Suggested fix (verified)

```diff
--- a/packages/expo-dev-menu/ios/FAB/DevMenuFABView.swift
+++ b/packages/expo-dev-menu/ios/FAB/DevMenuFABView.swift
@@ -185,6 +185,8 @@
         .animation(didPosition ? (isDragging ? dragSpring : FABConstants.snapAnimation) : nil, value: position)
     }
     .ignoresSafeArea()
+    // Positions are physical (they feed DevMenuFABWindow.hitTest), so never mirror them under RTL.
+    .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight)
   }
```

Applied to `node_modules/expo-dev-menu` in the repro and rebuilt: in Hebrew the gear is drawn top right, opens the menu, can be dragged and snaps to the edge, and taps elsewhere reach the app. The dev menu sheet itself stays RTL. The same code is still on `main`.

### Workaround

Turn the button off (the menu stays reachable by shake, or ⌃D with the simulator's hardware keyboard connected):
```
xcrun simctl spawn <udid> defaults write <bundle-id> EXDevMenuShowFloatingActionButton -bool false
```
then relaunch the app.

### Environment

- expo 57.0.31, expo-dev-client 57.0.20, expo-dev-menu 57.0.20, expo-dev-launcher 57.0.21, react-native 0.86.3 (New Architecture)
- Xcode 26.5 (17F42), iOS 26.5 Simulator: iPhone Air (420×912 pt); also seen on iPhone 17 (402×874 pt) in a larger app (expo-dev-menu 57.0.10)
- macOS 26.7.2, Node 23.11.0, CocoaPods 1.16.2

issue.body:
### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/colaquecez/expo-maps-mylocation-crash

### Steps to reproduce

**Platform:** Android only. iOS is unaffected.
**Environment:** development build (`npx expo run:android`). 
**Package manager:** npm.

### Steps

1. Clone the reproduction, `npm install`, then `npx expo run:android` on a physical device or an emulator with Google Play services.
2. Make sure the app holds no location permission. A fresh install already satisfies that; otherwise `adb shell pm revoke com.anonymous.repro android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` (and `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION`).
3. Launch the app. `App.tsx` renders a single `GoogleMaps.View` with `properties={{ isMyLocationEnabled: true }}` and nothing else.

**Expected:** the map renders without the blue dot, which is how iOS behaves with the identical prop.

**Actual:** the whole app crashes as soon as the map composes, with an unhandled `java.lang.SecurityException`. It is not an error surfaced to JS; the process dies.

```
java.lang.SecurityException: my location requires permission ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION or ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION
  com.google.android.gms.maps.internal.zzg.setMyLocationEnabled(com.google.android.gms:play-services-maps@@19.2.0:4)
  com.google.android.gms.maps.GoogleMap.setMyLocationEnabled(com.google.android.gms:play-services-maps@@19.2.0:1)
  com.google.maps.android.compose.MapUpdaterKt$MapUpdater$1$2$8.invoke(MapUpdater.kt:133)
  androidx.compose.runtime.Applier.apply(Applier.kt:180)
  ...
  androidx.compose.runtime.CompositionImpl.composeInitial(Composition.kt:732)
  androidx.compose.runtime.CompositionImpl.setContent(Composition.kt:699)
  com.google.maps.android.compose.GoogleMapKt$launchSubcomposition$1.invokeSuspend(GoogleMap.kt:252)
  ...
  android.app.ActivityThread.main(ActivityThread.java:10346)
```

The `composeInitial` / `setContent` frames show this is the map's first composition, so there is no point at which JS could catch it. No valid Google Maps API key is needed to reproduce: the crash happens in `setMyLocationEnabled`, before any tile is requested.

### Where it comes from

`expo-maps` passes the flag to `maps-compose` with no permission check, and the Android module has no permission check anywhere in it:

```kotlin
// android/src/main/java/expo/modules/maps/Records.kt
fun toMapProperties(): MapProperties {
  return MapProperties(
    isBuildingEnabled = isBuildingEnabled,
    isIndoorEnabled = isIndoorEnabled,
    isMyLocationEnabled = isMyLocationEnabled,   // <- no permission check
    ...
```

`maps-compose` then calls `GoogleMap.setMyLocationEnabled(true)` during composition, and the Maps SDK throws if neither `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` nor `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION` is held.

iOS handles the same prop safely. There it only decides whether a `UserAnnotation()` is rendered (`ios/AppleMapsViewiOS17.swift:99`, `ios/AppleMapsViewiOS18.swift:154`), which is a no-op without the permission rather than a crash. So the two platforms disagree about what the same prop does when the permission is missing.

### Why this is easy to hit in a real app

Any app that requests the location permission from the same screen that renders the map hits it. The map composes before the permission dialog is answered, so the first launch after a fresh install crashes.

The config plugin's `requestLocationPermission` option does not avoid it. That option only declares the permissions at build time and never requests anything at runtime.

`useLocationPermissions()` does not avoid it on its own either. It reads once on mount and has no listener, so a component that reads it on mount and then requests the permission elsewhere keeps a stale answer.

### Suggested fix

Either treat `isMyLocationEnabled` as `false` while the permission is missing, matching what iOS already does with the same prop, or document that the prop requires a granted permission so consumers know they must gate it themselves. A declarative prop should not be able to take the process down.

### Workaround

```tsx
const [permission] = Location.useForegroundPermissions();

<GoogleMaps.View
  properties={{ isMyLocationEnabled: permission?.granted ?? false }}
/>
```

Verified by A/B on a device: with the gate the app is stable; removing it reproduces the crash above with an identical stack.

issue.body:
### Minimal reproducible example
https://github.com/hrithik73/expo-audio-short-clip-repro

One screen (`App.tsx`) with a 0.2 s clip and a 1.0 s control clip. Open the app, wait about 3 s, then tap **Play short clip**: it's silent, though `didJustFinish` fires. A second tap is audible, and the 1.0 s clip is audible on its first play. The README includes the `dumpsys audio` output from the repro.

Refiling #52722 with the repro attached.

### Summary
On Android, if you create a player for a very short clip (under ~0.25–0.75 s, depending on the device's AudioTrack buffer) and call `play()` only after it has sat loaded for a few seconds, the first play is silent. The player still behaves as if it played: `playing` becomes `true`, `currentTime` reaches `duration`, and `didJustFinish` fires. Every later `seekTo(0)` + `play()` is audible. iOS is not affected.

This hits the common sound-effect pattern of preloading short UI or game sounds at startup and playing them later. In our app, the first bet, fold, card-deal and board-card sound of every session is silent.

```ts
const player = createAudioPlayer(require('./click-0.2s.mp3'))
setTimeout(() => player.play(), 3000) // silent on Android
// a later player.seekTo(0); player.play() is audible
```

**What happens (Pixel 7, Android 17):** `dumpsys audio` shows the player's AudioTrack being created during prepare, then `stopped` about 2 s later while still paused. It never logs `started`, and the first `play()` produces no output:

```
16:03:24.168 new player piid:4735 ... type:android.media.AudioTrack
16:03:26.166 player piid:4735 event:stopped        <- before play() was called
16:03:27.209 play() from JS                          <- no "started" event
```

Affected on this device: clips of 0.13, 0.18, 0.21, 0.24 and 0.31 s. Not affected: 0.42, 0.52 and 0.73 s.

**Root cause (Media3 1.9.1):** a clip that fits entirely in the sink buffer reaches output end of stream while the player is paused. The renderer then calls `DefaultAudioSink.playToEndOfStream()` → `playPendingData()` → `AudioOutput.stop()`, without checking whether playback ever started. A stream-mode AudioTrack that is stopped before it is played never outputs its pending data. An upstream report to androidx/media will be linked here.

Calling `pause()` + `seekTo(0)` before the first `play()` does not help; it is still silent. Our app-side workaround is to play each short clip once at volume 0 right after it loads, so the broken first play happens silently.

### Environment
- Repro app: expo 58.0.22, expo-audio 58.0.11, react-native 0.88.1
- Also seen in our production app: expo 58.0.19, expo-audio 58.0.10, react-native 0.88.0 (new architecture)
- Media3 1.9.1
- Device: Google Pixel 7, Android 17 (API 37)

issue.title: [audio] Start playback when the item becomes ready after play()

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

`AVPlayer.playImmediately(atRate:)` is a no-op while the current `AVPlayerItem` is not yet ready to play. When JS calls `play()` immediately after creating a player for a remote/live stream, the call is silently dropped and the player stays paused until some other event restarts it.

# How

- Track the playback intent in `playWanted`.
- When `play(at:)` is called before the item is ready, defer the start through the existing `onReady` helper (already used by `replaceCurrentSource` / `handleMediaServicesReset`) instead of calling `playImmediately` immediately.
- `pause()` clears `playWanted` so a late readiness cannot start audio against the user's wish; `resumePlayback()` re-arms it.

No public API or JS-side changes.

# Test Plan

Tested with the `expo-audio` example app on iOS:

1. Create a player for a remote stream and call `play()` immediately, before the item finishes loading.
   - Before: stays paused. After: playback starts as soon as the item is ready.
2. `play()` then `pause()` before the item is ready → stays paused when it loads.
3. Loop / seek / playback-rate behavior unchanged once loaded.

comment.body:
Hi @rmotafreitas, thanks for the PR.

I could not reproduce the root cause. I created an `AVPlayer` and called `playImmediately(atRate: 1.0)` right away, before the item was ready. I tried a remote MP3 and an HLS stream. In both cases the rate stayed at `1.0`, the player waited while the item loaded, and playback started when the item became ready. I tested this on macOS, not on iOS.

`play()` on `main` also calls `playImmediately` directly, and nothing resets the rate when the item becomes ready. So I don't think the call is dropped in the way the PR describes.

Can you share a minimal repro that fails on `main`? Please include:

- The source URL, or the type of stream (for example, Icecast, HLS, or a plain file)
- The code that creates the player and calls `play()`
- Any other calls on the player between `play()` and the item becoming ready, for example `replace()` or `seekTo()`
- The iOS version and whether you used a device or a simulator

One path that can drop playback is a call to `replace()` while the player is still waiting to play. If your app does that, it could explain what you saw. It would need a different fix.

2. In a second terminal run `npx expo run:android`.

issue.title: [audio][android] Report the stream state at queue time and drop buffers from a stopped session

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

Fixes #52262.

On Android, `AudioStream` posts its events to the main queue and reads the stream state when the queued block runs, not when it was queued. Two things go wrong:

- `emitStatus()` reads `isStreaming` inside the block. If `stop()` runs before the block queued by `start()`, both status events report `false`.
- `emitBufferEvent()` never checks whether the session that recorded the buffer is still running. A buffer queued just before `stop()` is delivered after the next `start()`, so the new session begins with audio from the old one.

# How

- `emitStatus()` captures `isStreaming` into a local before queueing the event, and the block emits that value.
- Each `start()` increments a `session` counter. `startCaptureLoop()` captures the counter once, and every buffer read by that loop carries it to `emitBufferEvent()`. The queued block returns early when the stream is no longer streaming or the counter has changed. Capturing in the loop, not at emit time, matters: the new `start()` can increment the counter between a blocking `read()` returning and the emit, and a buffer tagged at emit time would then get the new number. `isStreaming` and `session` are `@Volatile`, because the block runs on the main thread while `start()` and `stop()` run on other threads.
- The chunk being read when `stop()` is called is discarded. That is what the issue asks for. The alternative, gating only on the session, keeps that chunk after a plain `stop()` but also delivers it after an immediate restart, because when it is queued nothing knows whether a restart follows. On the emulator that variant delivered the old chunk after 10 of 10 restarts.
- No new allocations or locks. The cost is one captured value and two comparisons per event.

This is a single pull request, not a stack.

# Test Plan

Ran a standalone SDK 58 app with `expo-audio` 58.0.10 on the Android 17 emulator (API 37), with `expo-audio` built from the `node_modules` sources (`expo.autolinking.buildFromSource`) so the patched Kotlin is compiled in. App and results: https://github.com/dileepapeiris/expo-audio-stream-events-repro

Case 2, old buffer after a restart: await `start()`, record for 1.2 s, then call `stop()` and `await start()` back to back and watch for 0.6 s. A buffer from the stopped session has a native `timestamp` of about 1.2 s; one from the new session stays under 0.9 s.

- Before: an old buffer after every restart.
- After: 1 of 10 restarts. That one buffer had already been emitted to JavaScript before `stop()` ran and reached the JavaScript thread 1 ms after `stop()` returned. A native check cannot retract an event that was already handed over.

Case 3, plain `stop()`: await `start()`, wait for a buffer, call `stop()`, count buffers in the next 0.5 s.

- Before: 1 buffer after every `stop()`, 5 of 5.
- After: 0 of 5. See How for why this is the chosen behaviour.

Case 1, status after `start()` and `stop()`: await `start()`, call `stop()`, collect the status events for one second.

- Before and after: `[true, false]` in 5 of 5 runs. From JavaScript this path does not reproduce, because `start()` is an `AsyncFunction` and the queued `true` block has run before `stop()` is called. The `[false, false]` in the report comes from calling the native `start()` and `stop()` on the same thread back to back, which the reporter's JVM harness does. The captured value makes that path report the state at queue time.

Not run: `et check-packages expo-audio`, this machine cannot install the monorepo. The native change has no unit-test seam, so the steps above are the test.

# Screenshots

No UI change.

### Minimal reproducible example

[Reproduction code](https://github.com/qq382724935/react-native-sdk-regression-repros/tree/main/expo-audio) — expo-audio 58.0.10, Android.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Hold the event queue in the reproduction fixture.
2. Start and stop a stream, then drain the queue: status events are `[false, false]`.
3. Queue one PCM buffer, stop and restart the stream, then drain the queue: the previous recording's buffer is delivered.

Run the `status_snapshot` and `stale_buffer` cases with `python3 android/run.py --package-dir sdk/package --case CASE --download-tools`.

**Expected:** Status events preserve `[true, false]`. Buffers from a stopped recording are discarded.

**Actual:** Queued status reads the later state; queued PCM is delivered even after its recording has ended.

### Relevant code

```kotlin
appContext?.mainQueue?.launch {
  emit(AUDIO_STREAM_STATUS, mapOf("isStreaming" to isStreaming))
```

issue.title: [audio][android] Report the stream state at queue time and drop buffers from a stopped session

labels.name: repo-0a721bb5
labels.description: PR author is not a member of the expo GitHub org

issue.body:
# Why

Fixes #52262.

On Android, `AudioStream` posts its events to the main queue and reads the stream state when the queued block runs, not when it was queued. Two things go wrong:

- `emitStatus()` reads `isStreaming` inside the block. If `stop()` runs before the block queued by `start()`, both status events report `false`.
- `emitBufferEvent()` never checks whether the session that recorded the buffer is still running. A buffer queued just before `stop()` is delivered after the next `start()`, so the new session begins with audio from the old one.

# How

- `emitStatus()` captures `isStreaming` into a local before queueing the event, and the block emits that value.
- Each `start()` increments a `session` counter. `startCaptureLoop()` captures the counter once, and every buffer read by that loop carries it to `emitBufferEvent()`. The queued block returns early when the stream is no longer streaming or the counter has changed. Capturing in the loop, not at emit time, matters: the new `start()` can increment the counter between a blocking `read()` returning and the emit, and a buffer tagged at emit time would then get the new number. `isStreaming` and `session` are `@Volatile`, because the block runs on the main thread while `start()` and `stop()` run on other threads.
- The chunk being read when `stop()` is called is discarded. That is what the issue asks for. The alternative, gating only on the session, keeps that chunk after a plain `stop()` but also delivers it after an immediate restart, because when it is queued nothing knows whether a restart follows. On the emulator that variant delivered the old chunk after 10 of 10 restarts.
- No new allocations or locks. The cost is one captured value and two comparisons per event.

This is a single pull request, not a stack.

# Test Plan

Ran a standalone SDK 58 app with `expo-audio` 58.0.10 on the Android 17 emulator (API 37), with `expo-audio` built from the `node_modules` sources (`expo.autolinking.buildFromSource`) so the patched Kotlin is compiled in. App and results: https://github.com/dileepapeiris/expo-audio-stream-events-repro

Case 2, old buffer after a restart: await `start()`, record for 1.2 s, then call `stop()` and `await start()` back to back and watch for 0.6 s. A buffer from the stopped session has a native `timestamp` of about 1.2 s; one from the new session stays under 0.9 s.

- Before: an old buffer after every restart.
- After: 1 of 10 restarts. That one buffer had already been emitted to JavaScript before `stop()` ran and reached the JavaScript thread 1 ms after `stop()` returned. A native check cannot retract an event that was already handed over.

Case 3, plain `stop()`: await `start()`, wait for a buffer, call `stop()`, count buffers in the next 0.5 s.

- Before: 1 buffer after every `stop()`, 5 of 5.
- After: 0 of 5. See How for why this is the chosen behaviour.

Case 1, status after `start()` and `stop()`: await `start()`, call `stop()`, collect the status events for one second.

- Before and after: `[true, false]` in 5 of 5 runs. From JavaScript this path does not reproduce, because `start()` is an `AsyncFunction` and the queued `true` block has run before `stop()` is called. The `[false, false]` in the report comes from calling the native `start()` and `stop()` on the same thread back to back, which the reporter's JVM harness does. The captured value makes that path report the state at queue time.

Not run: `et check-packages expo-audio`, this machine cannot install the monorepo. The native change has no unit-test seam, so the steps above are the test.

# Screenshots

No UI change.

---

### Steps to reproduce

Platform: iOS (physical device). Environment: Release build with the SDK 57 defaults (precompiled Expo modules). Package manager: npm.

1. Clone the repository, run `npm install`, then `npx expo prebuild -p ios`.
2. Look at the `pod install` output and at the bundled `libavif` binary:


   ```sh
   # AOMedia Project AV1 Encoder 3.0.0

   ```

3. Run the app on an iPhone in Release (`npx expo run:ios --configuration Release --device`) and watch the Xcode memory gauge. Scroll the list to the end (30 pages), then open a detail and tap "Next detail ›" 10 times.
4. Add `"expo": { "autolinking": { "ios": { "buildFromSource": ["expo-image"] } } }` to `package.json`, run `pod install`, and repeat step 3. `pod install` now installs `libdav1d (1.2.0)`, as `ExpoImage.podspec` requests (`s.dependency 'libavif/libdav1d' unless disable_libdav1d`).

| Point | Precompiled (libaom) | `buildFromSource` (libdav1d) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App open | ~71 MB | ~70 MB |
| Page 10 of the list | ~400 MB | ~100 MB |
| End of the list (page 30) | ~800 MB | ~124 MB |
| After stacking 10 details | ~1.3 GB | ~100 MB |
| Peak | ~1.6 GB, then a critical memory warning | ~120 MB |

**Impact in production:** our app shows AVIF photos in long image lists, with a FlashList of photo carousels per card plus stacked detail screens. Since we moved to SDK 57, iOS kills it while it is in the foreground (`WatchdogTermination`, no JS error or native crash report). Pods installed per build, from the EAS install-pods logs:

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 54 | 3.0.11 (source) | `libavif` + `libdav1d 1.2.0` | no terminations |
| B | 57 | 57.0.5 (precompiled) | `libavif` (libaom 3.0.0) | terminated after scrolling ~30 pages + opening a detail |
| C | 57 | 57.0.5 + `buildFromSource` | `libavif` + `libdav1d 1.2.0` | no terminations |

**Workaround we shipped:**

```json
"expo": {
  "autolinking": {
    "ios": { "buildFromSource": ["expo-image", "expo-image-manipulator"] }
```

issue.body:
### Minimal reproducible example
https://github.com/hrithik73/expo-audio-short-clip-repro

One screen (`App.tsx`) with a 0.2 s clip and a 1.0 s control clip. Open the app, wait about 3 s, then tap **Play short clip**: it's silent, though `didJustFinish` fires. A second tap is audible, and the 1.0 s clip is audible on its first play. The README includes the `dumpsys audio` output from the repro.

Refiling #52722 with the repro attached.

### Summary
On Android, if you create a player for a very short clip (under ~0.25–0.75 s, depending on the device's AudioTrack buffer) and call `play()` only after it has sat loaded for a few seconds, the first play is silent. The player still behaves as if it played: `playing` becomes `true`, `currentTime` reaches `duration`, and `didJustFinish` fires. Every later `seekTo(0)` + `play()` is audible. iOS is not affected.

This hits the common sound-effect pattern of preloading short UI or game sounds at startup and playing them later. In our app, the first bet, fold, card-deal and board-card sound of every session is silent.

```ts
const player = createAudioPlayer(require('./click-0.2s.mp3'))
setTimeout(() => player.play(), 3000) // silent on Android
// a later player.seekTo(0); player.play() is audible
```

**What happens (Pixel 7, Android 17):** `dumpsys audio` shows the player's AudioTrack being created during prepare, then `stopped` about 2 s later while still paused. It never logs `started`, and the first `play()` produces no output:

```
16:03:24.168 new player piid:4735 ... type:android.media.AudioTrack
16:03:26.166 player piid:4735 event:stopped        <- before play() was called
16:03:27.209 play() from JS                          <- no "started" event
```

Affected on this device: clips of 0.13, 0.18, 0.21, 0.24 and 0.31 s. Not affected: 0.42, 0.52 and 0.73 s.

**Root cause (Media3 1.9.1):** a clip that fits entirely in the sink buffer reaches output end of stream while the player is paused. The renderer then calls `DefaultAudioSink.playToEndOfStream()` → `playPendingData()` → `AudioOutput.stop()`, without checking whether playback ever started. A stream-mode AudioTrack that is stopped before it is played never outputs its pending data. An upstream report to androidx/media will be linked here.

Calling `pause()` + `seekTo(0)` before the first `play()` does not help; it is still silent. Our app-side workaround is to play each short clip once at volume 0 right after it loads, so the broken first play happens silently.

### Environment
- Repro app: expo 58.0.22, expo-audio 58.0.11, react-native 0.88.1
- Also seen in our production app: expo 58.0.19, expo-audio 58.0.10, react-native 0.88.0 (new architecture)
- Media3 1.9.1
- Device: Google Pixel 7, Android 17 (API 37)

issue.body:
### Minimal reproducible example
https://github.com/hrithik73/expo-audio-short-clip-repro

One screen (`App.tsx`) with a 0.2 s clip and a 1.0 s control clip. Open the app, wait about 3 s, then tap **Play short clip**: it's silent, though `didJustFinish` fires. A second tap is audible, and the 1.0 s clip is audible on its first play. The README includes the `dumpsys audio` output from the repro.

Refiling #52722 with the repro attached.

### Summary
On Android, if you create a player for a very short clip (under ~0.25–0.75 s, depending on the device's AudioTrack buffer) and call `play()` only after it has sat loaded for a few seconds, the first play is silent. The player still behaves as if it played: `playing` becomes `true`, `currentTime` reaches `duration`, and `didJustFinish` fires. Every later `seekTo(0)` + `play()` is audible. iOS is not affected.

This hits the common sound-effect pattern of preloading short UI or game sounds at startup and playing them later. In our app, the first bet, fold, card-deal and board-card sound of every session is silent.

```ts
const player = createAudioPlayer(require('./click-0.2s.mp3'))
setTimeout(() => player.play(), 3000) // silent on Android
// a later player.seekTo(0); player.play() is audible
```

**What happens (Pixel 7, Android 17):** `dumpsys audio` shows the player's AudioTrack being created during prepare, then `stopped` about 2 s later while still paused. It never logs `started`, and the first `play()` produces no output:

```
16:03:24.168 new player piid:4735 ... type:android.media.AudioTrack
16:03:26.166 player piid:4735 event:stopped        <- before play() was called
16:03:27.209 play() from JS                          <- no "started" event
```

Affected on this device: clips of 0.13, 0.18, 0.21, 0.24 and 0.31 s. Not affected: 0.42, 0.52 and 0.73 s.

**Root cause (Media3 1.9.1):** a clip that fits entirely in the sink buffer reaches output end of stream while the player is paused. The renderer then calls `DefaultAudioSink.playToEndOfStream()` → `playPendingData()` → `AudioOutput.stop()`, without checking whether playback ever started. A stream-mode AudioTrack that is stopped before it is played never outputs its pending data. An upstream report to androidx/media will be linked here.

Calling `pause()` + `seekTo(0)` before the first `play()` does not help; it is still silent. Our app-side workaround is to play each short clip once at volume 0 right after it loads, so the broken first play happens silently.

### Environment
- Repro app: expo 58.0.22, expo-audio 58.0.11, react-native 0.88.1
- Also seen in our production app: expo 58.0.19, expo-audio 58.0.10, react-native 0.88.0 (new architecture)
- Media3 1.9.1
- Device: Google Pixel 7, Android 17 (API 37)

issue.body:
# Why

On first launch, the launcher view controller is not part of the view controller hierarchy. So it gets no safe area and no system layout margins. With the system navigation bar from #52530, the large title and toolbar items sit on the screen edge on iOS 26. This is the same root cause as #42540 and #43672.

# How

When its view is the window root's view, the launcher view controller now becomes a child of the window root. It never detaches, because the app it loads later reuses it under the same parent (#43520). SwiftUI's selected tab only gets a safe area after it appears, so the launcher runs an appearance pass after it installs its hosting controller. The #42540 workaround now runs only while the launcher has no parent.

# Test Plan

On the iPhone 17 (iOS 26.5) simulator and a physical device, the first launch shows correct margins and safe areas. A `fullScreenModal` with `router.back()` does not freeze (#43520). I checked this on launcher-first, auto-launch, and second launches. Rotation, per-screen orientation (#44181), and component switching (#46613) still work. In a SwiftUI host the launcher does not attach.

issue.body:
### Summary

On iOS 26.0 (simulator), the results of every `AsyncFunction` are converted to JavaScript on a Swift cooperative-pool thread instead of the JavaScript thread. This happens while Hermes is running on the JS thread, so the two threads race inside the runtime. It corrupts the heap and crashes with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`: sometimes cleanly inside JSI, sometimes at a garbage address on the JS thread.

The cause appears to be `JavaScriptRuntime.Scheduler.execute(_:) async` in `expo-modules-jsi`. It dispatches to the JS thread correctly with `scheduleTask`, then runs the closure through `Task.immediate_polyfill { @JavaScriptActor in ... }`. On iOS 26 that is `Task.immediate`, which does not start on the JS thread. The job goes to the global concurrent executor instead of `JavaScriptExecutor`.

### Evidence

**1. `Task.immediate` vs `Task` from the JS thread.** We added logging to `AppContext.setRuntime(_:scheduler:dispatch:)`, which runs on `com.facebook.react.runtime.JavaScript`:

```swift
Task.immediate_polyfill(priority: .high) { @JavaScriptActor in log("polyfill") }
Task(priority: .high) { @JavaScriptActor in log("plain Task") }
if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { Task.immediate { @JavaScriptActor in log("Task.immediate") } }
log("after creating tasks")
```

Output (thread id / pthread name):

```
after Task.immediate_polyfill returned  tid=…975 com.facebook.react.runtime.JavaScript
Task.immediate_polyfill body            tid=…936 (unnamed)            <- later, pool thread
plain Task body                         tid=…975 com.facebook.react.runtime.JavaScript  <- synchronous, correct
after creating tasks                    tid=…975 com.facebook.react.runtime.JavaScript
Task.immediate body                     tid=…936 (unnamed)            <- later, pool thread
```

A plain `Task` goes through `JavaScriptExecutor.enqueue`, which runs the job synchronously on the JS thread as intended. `Task.immediate` returns first and then runs the body on a pool thread.

**2. `AsyncFunction` results.** We logged inside the `appContext.runtime.execute { ... }` closure in `ConcurrentFunctionDefinition.call`:

```
setRuntime scheduler=true dispatch=true   tid=…805 com.facebook.react.runtime.JavaScript
getPendingInvocationsAsync  inExecute tid=…698 (unnamed)  isOnJavaScriptThread()=false
getCurrentPositionAsync     inExecute tid=…699 (unnamed)  isOnJavaScriptThread()=false
reverseGeocodeAsync         inExecute tid=…699 (unnamed)  isOnJavaScriptThread()=false
```

The React runtime scheduler is bound (`scheduler=true`), yet `isOnJavaScriptThread()` is false inside the closure that `execute` is meant to run on the JS thread.

**3. Crash.** `Location.reverseGeocodeAsync` (which returns `[[String: Any?]]`) loses the race reliably in our app. Faulting thread, with the JS thread concurrently inside `hermesvm`:

```
EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x00000000000000c0
Thread 27 (unnamed):
  hermesvm
  ExpoModulesJSI  facebook::jsi::PropNameID::forUtf8(facebook::jsi::IRuntime&, ...)   jsi.h:880
  ExpoModulesJSI  String.toJSIPropNameID(in:)                                        String+JSI.swift:59
  ExpoModulesJSI  JavaScriptObject.setProperty(_:value:)                             JavaScriptObject.swift:308
  …               DynamicDictionaryType.convertToJS(_:appContext:in:)                DynamicDictionaryType.swift:94
  …               DynamicArrayType.convertToJS(_:appContext:in:)                     DynamicArrayType.swift:86
  …               MainValueConverter.toJS(_:_:)                                      MainValueConverter.swift:43
  …               closure #1 in ConcurrentFunctionDefinition.call(_:argumentsTuple:) ConcurrentFunctionDefinition.swift:76
  ExpoModulesJSI  closure #1 in JavaScriptRuntime.execute(_:)                        JavaScriptRuntime.swift:646
  ExpoModulesJSI  closure #1 in closure #1 in closure #2 in Scheduler.execute(_:)    JavaScriptRuntimeScheduler.swift:210
  libswift_Concurrency
Thread 5 (com.facebook.react.runtime.JavaScript):
  hermesvm …
```

Other crashes from the same trigger fault on the JS thread inside `hermesvm` at garbage addresses (for example `0x000000037044774b`), which is consistent with heap corruption from the concurrent access.

### Suggested fix

In `JavaScriptRuntimeScheduler.swift`, inside the `scheduleTask` callback (already on the JS thread), avoid relying on `Task.immediate` honouring the custom `JavaScriptActor` executor. Either:
- use `Task { @JavaScriptActor in ... }`, whose enqueue on `JavaScriptExecutor` runs synchronously on the calling (JS) thread, or
- call the closure inside `JavaScriptActor.assumeIsolated` when it has no suspension points.

`Task.immediate_polyfill` is also used on the inline path (line ~203) and in the blocking `execute`. Those likely need the same review.

### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/tadeegan/expo-task-immediate-repro

It's a blank `create-expo-app` SDK 58 template plus one local module (`modules/thread-probe`), using Expo's precompiled iOS binaries unmodified.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install && npx expo run:ios` on the iOS 26.0 simulator.
2. Tap **1. Run thread probes**. `Task { @JavaScriptActor }` reports `com.facebook.react.runtime.JavaScript`, while `Task.immediate { @JavaScriptActor }` and `Task.immediate_polyfill { @JavaScriptActor }` report an unnamed pool thread.
3. Tap **2. Stress AsyncFunction results**. This calls an `AsyncFunction` returning `[[String: Any?]]`, 20 at a time, while JS is busy. The app crashes within seconds with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` on an unnamed thread: `hermesvm` ← `ExpoModulesJSI` ← `ExpoModulesCore` ← `ExpoModulesJSI` ← `libswift_Concurrency`.

In a real app, `Location.reverseGeocodeAsync` called as a map screen mounts crashes the same way every time.

### Environment

- expo 58.0.20, expo-modules-core 58.0.27, expo-modules-jsi 58.0.20 (prebuilt xcframework), expo-location 58.0.19, expo-router 58.0.27
- `Scheduler.execute`, `Task.immediate_polyfill` and `JavaScriptExecutor` are unchanged in expo-modules-jsi 58.0.21. That release could not be built on Xcode 26.0.1 to confirm: its sources are rebuilt and fail with `sending 'slot' risks causing data races`.
- react-native 0.88.0 (prebuilt React-Core), New Architecture / bridgeless, Hermes
- Xcode 26.0.1, Swift 6.2 (swiftlang-6.2.0.19.9); `ExpoModulesJSI.swiftinterface` reports the same compiler
- iOS 26.0 simulator (23A343), macOS 15.7.1
- Not yet tested on iOS 26.1+ runtimes or physical devices. We see no matching crashes from physical devices in production.
